actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Seed of the environment's random generator
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

inputs.description: Seed used by the next reset
inputs.name: seed

facts.text: The registered environment ids are built for every scenario name as GFootball-{env_name}-SMM-v0, GFootball-{env_name}-Pixels-v0, GFootball-{env_name}-simple115-v0 and GFootball-{env_name}-simple115v2-v0, with entry point gfootball.env:create_environment
create_environment constructs football_env.FootballEnv(c) and calls _apply_output_wrappers before returning it
The output wrapper chain applies the reward, representation, single-agent and GetState wrappers
FootballEnv.action_space is Discrete(action-set length) when one player is agent-controlled
The default action set is action_set_v1: 19 actions from idle through release_dribble
The simple115 observation is a Box with 115 values per controlled player, float32, bounds -inf to inf

The simple115 layout is 88 player values (backfilled with -1 when fewer than 11 players), then the ball position array, the ball direction array, a 3-value possession one-hot, 11 active-player flags and 7 game-mode flags
The raw observation's ball position and ball direction are each arrays of three values
The 11_vs_11_stochastic scenario sets game_duration 3000 and deterministic False
The episode is done when the step count reaches game_duration
FootballEnv.step returns observation, reward, done and info; reset returns the observation
The engine runs 100 physics steps per second
The default config advances 10 physics steps per frame
The default config is not real-time paced (real_time False)
The default config's player list is agent:left_players=1
FootballEnvCore.reset starts a new episode and resets the action set and step counter

determinism.notes: the 11_vs_11_stochastic scenario sets deterministic False and the engine seed is drawn with random.randint (scenario_builder.py:80-88); the package's fake is a repeatable stand-in but the upstream reset() takes no seed or options, so no determinism claim is made

gaps: no game engine: the fake is a kinematic stand-in that moves a placeholder ball; it models no players, contacts, goals, physics, rendering or the C++ engine and was never compared with an upstream run
players are not modelled: the 88 player values keep the upstream backfill value -1 and the active-player one-hot is all zeros
no reward is modelled: every step returns 0.0, so goals and score changes are absent
one tick is one frame: 100 ms at the default 10 physics steps per frame and 100 physics steps per second; no wall-clock pacing (realtime_factor 0)
the upstream reset() takes no seed or options and the fake matches that signature: the bridge's cap.world.seed.v1 and reset seed are recorded but cannot change the episode
snapshot and restore are not offered: the fake does not implement the upstream get_state/set_state, so fidelity snapshot_restore is false

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
